reader_question: How did each state vote in 2024, and how did that compare with 2020?
grade_line: Documented: official results the states reported, compiled by the Federal Election Commission
title: The Republican nominee led in 31 states in 2024, six more than in 2020; in four of the six states that changed leader, the lead was under 2.5 points.
reading_guide: Each margin sits on the side of the nominee who led, with the party named: left of the center line, the Democratic nominee; right of it, the Republican nominee. Bars grow from the center line, and every arrow points toward the Republican nominee.
measure_line: Presidential margin by state in 2024 and 2020: the leading nominee’s share of all presidential votes minus the other’s, in percentage points, with the shift between the two elections; 50 states and DC, with the United States above them
notes: Margin: the Republican nominee’s share of all presidential votes minus the Democratic nominee’s, printed as the leader’s lead. A state whose leader changed carries a tag.
The Democratic nominee led in 19 states and DC in 2024. The four close changes of leader: Wisconsin Republican +0.9, Michigan Republican +1.4, Pennsylvania Republican +1.7, Georgia Republican +2.2.
New York’s figures count every ballot line each nominee held, including the Working Families and Conservative lines.
Maine and Nebraska split their electoral votes by district; these margins are statewide.
source_line: Source: Federal Election Commission, Federal Elections 2020 (Table 2) and Official 2024 Presidential General Election Results, compiled from state election offices, November 2020 and November 2024, 50 states and DC. Retrieved November 6, 2026. Margins are Republican minus Democratic share of all presidential votes; New York counts fused party lines.
alt: A results table of every state and DC, with the United States above them, giving the 2024 and 2020 presidential margins with the leader named and the shift toward the Republican nominee. The Republican nominee led in 31 states in 2024, six more than in 2020: Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Georgia by under 2.5 points, Nevada by 3.1 and Arizona by 5.5.

table.caption: Presidential margin and vote shares, the United States and each state, 2024 and 2020

columns.label: Shift toward the Republican nominee, points

chart_notes: Each margin sits on the side of the nominee who led, with the party named. Bars grow from the center line; arrows give the shift toward the Republican nominee. The rows run in order of the 2024 margin, with a line where the leader changes. On phones each row shows the 2024 margin and the shift, and the 2020 margin is in this table.
phone_note: On phones each row shows the state, its 2024 margin with the leader named and the shift toward the Republican nominee beside its arrow; the 2020 margin is in the table equivalent.

labels.even_line: Even line. In every row above, the Democratic nominee led in 2024; in every row below, the Republican nominee led.
